# Codex exec image observability audit, 2026-09-26

This audit makes no model call. It inspects the already-installed CLI's generated app-server schema and binary discriminant strings, then the official source for its matching release tag. The first web lookup used an incorrect source filename and returned404; the corrected source and immutable commit are recorded in provenance.json.

The installed CLI is0.153.4; its exact path/hash are in provenance.json. Official `rust-v0.153.4` resolves to `3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a`. This is a release-source association, not a reproducible-build attestation of the installed binary.

The locally generated ItemCompletedNotification schema permits `imageView` with id/path and `imageGeneration` with result/status/savedPath. In contrast, the release [exec event enum](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a/codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs#L107) has no image-view, image-generation or dynamic-tool-call variant. The installed binary's exec event discriminants are consistent with that narrower enum. The [JSONL mapper](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a/codex-rs/exec/src/event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs#L143) maps selected app-server items and returns None for the rest at line316. Both started and completed item handling use that mapper, and notifications emit only mapped items (lines338–361 and470–485).

Consequently, missing image-view events in this exec JSON capture are expected even if such views occurred. This stream cannot establish that the model did not view images, nor prove that it did. Numeric content measurements through a visible shell command could still be established from their command/result payload; none appears in the reviewed video turn. Generated PNGs and the later independent decoder prove output artifacts/properties, not in-turn image inspection.

The reporting criterion is therefore **unverified with this capture interface**, not a demonstrated false-inspection claim. The earlier original-render reporting-failure classification remains historical, but its causal assertion that the model did not inspect is unsupported by this event stream. Do not erase that record, convert it to a pass, invent a hidden view, or award the frozen in-turn-evidence requirement from a later oracle. The same limitation applies to completeness of tool counts and image-generation counts obtained from this CLI JSON interface.

No source repair, retry, new model trial or protocol replacement is authorized or performed by this audit. A future observed-image criterion would need an explicitly reviewed capture interface that preserves those notifications, or an authorized visible decoded-content measurement; this is a coverage requirement, not permission to rerun.
